stem: During community vaccine education, which statement by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: Vaccination has prevented large numbers of illnesses, hospitalizations, and deaths, and staying up to date remains important because vaccine-preventable diseases can persist or reemerge when protection is insufficient.
options.B: Successful vaccination programs eliminate the need for continued immunization once disease incidence becomes low.
options.C: Vaccines are relevant mainly to diseases that no longer circulate and therefore provide little current public-health benefit.
options.D: Once a vaccine-preventable disease is controlled locally, surveillance and continued vaccination are unnecessary.

rationale: A is correct. CDC reports that routine childhood vaccination has prevented hundreds of millions of illnesses and millions of hospitalizations and deaths in the United States. CDC also emphasizes that serious vaccine-preventable diseases remain a threat and that continued vaccination is needed to maintain protection and prevent reemergence or outbreaks. B and D ignore the need to sustain coverage after disease control or elimination targets are reached. C is false because multiple vaccine-preventable diseases continue to circulate and cause morbidity and mortality.
educational_objective: Explain that vaccination has substantially reduced vaccine-preventable disease burden, but continued age- and risk-appropriate vaccination and surveillance remain necessary to preserve protection and prevent resurgence.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Vaccines and the Diseases they Prevent; Vaccine-Preventable Diseases — Global Immunization; Routine Immunizations on Schedule for Everyone (RISE)
source_version_date: Vaccines and Diseases dated August 10, 2024; Global VPD page current 2024–2026; RISE dated May 4, 2026; accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Vaccines and the Diseases they Prevent — routine vaccinations for children born 1994–2023 are estimated to prevent about 508 million illnesses, 32 million hospitalizations, and over 1.1 million deaths. Global Immunization — elimination/control sections: continued disease detection and vaccination are required to maintain elimination targets and prevent reemergence. RISE — routine immunization coverage remains an active public-health priority to protect against vaccine-preventable disease and disability.
source_claim_supported: Vaccines have substantially reduced disease burden and saved lives, but ongoing recommended vaccination and surveillance remain necessary because vaccine-preventable diseases persist and can reemerge when coverage declines.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance: provide immunization education, promote preventive health practices, and reinforce age- and risk-appropriate vaccination.
blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — vaccine-preventable disease education
correction_summary: Rebuilt the broad historical-impact item into a current prevention message with directly supported CDC outcome data and the essential maintenance principle that low disease incidence does not eliminate the need for vaccination or surveillance.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against current CDC vaccination-impact and disease-control resources, including 2026 RISE materials.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A combines demonstrated disease-burden reduction with continued vaccination need. B and D incorrectly stop prevention after success. C denies ongoing VPD burden.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; control success depends on maintaining vaccination.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; vaccine-preventable diseases still circulate and cause harm.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; surveillance and vaccination remain important after disease reduction.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A accurately integrates both historical/current benefit and ongoing prevention needs.
audit_findings.cueing: All options address the public-health implications of vaccination.
audit_findings.blueprint: Preventive vaccination education fits Health Promotion and Maintenance.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked current CDC impact estimates and avoided claiming that vaccines guarantee eradication or that all diseases require identical schedules. No second answer remained.
